A.rule: throughput shortfall without a slow consumer component

report.summary: Outbox publication fell far behind arrivals in the later part of the window, growing the pending backlog. The consumer handler is slow on some attempts (p95 ~1.2 s), the likely bottleneck, but a direct time link is missing.

findings.claim: Publications fell to about 6-8 per 10 s against 30 arrivals per 10 s in the later buckets, so pending grew from ~4 to 171 and notifications were delayed.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show a sustained gap; pending samples rise 4 -> 97 -> 171 while arrivals stay steady.

findings.claim: Delay inside delivery comes from the consumer handler (p95 1205 ms, max 1205 ms). Consumer auth (~71 ms) and LedgerCore overhead are small.
findings.reason: Total p95 1277 ms is almost entirely consumer handler time; handler p50 is only 0.022 ms, so a subset of calls is slow.

findings.claim: Slow consumer calls, if processed one batch at a time, would cap throughput well below the arrival rate and build the backlog; this link is inferred.
findings.reason: The 1 s poll interval and batch size of 20 plus ~1.2 s calls fit the reduced rate, but serialization and timing of the slow calls were not shown.

limitations: No data on when the consumer slowdown started relative to the publication drop, so the time link is not shown.
Delivery log listing covers only the earliest 100 of 513 records, so the later slow period is not listed.
next_checks: Get per-bucket consumer handler latency over time and compare it with the drop in publications at the 12th bucket.

alternatives.reason: Pool had 0 pending and 0 timeouts, and there were no blocking sessions in 105 samples.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database contention or pool exhaustion slowed the publisher.

alternatives.reason: The failed count is constant at 778 through the window, so it is a pre-existing static backlog, not new failures.
